help.apm: Actions per minute, from the replay.
help.army: What your army was worth then, in the game's score.
help.armyTrade: Army you killed for each army you lost, by the game's score. Above 1 means you traded well.
help.baseLead: Your bases minus your opponent's at 10 minutes. Below 0 means they were on more.
help.buildTiming: When you usually start it, compared to other players.
help.detection: When you first started something that sees cloaked and burrowed units: an Observer or Photon Cannon, or a Missile Turret, Comsat Station or Science Vessel. Games without one are left out.
help.eapmPhase: Effective actions per minute: actions that did something, leaving out spam.
help.hotkeyJumps: Times a minute you double tapped a hotkey to move your screen to that group, from the replay.
help.hotkeys: Times a minute you selected a hotkeyed group, from the replay.
help.larvaeFull: The share of the first 10 minutes your Hatcheries, Lairs and Hives spent holding three larvae, when they stop making more. Every larva they would have made is one you never get.
help.mining: Minerals and gas you mined in the minute before that point.
help.overlordsLostRate: Overlords of yours that died, for every 10 minutes you played.
help.phases: The early game is up to 6 minutes, the mid game 6 to 12, and the late game after that.
help.production: Barracks, Factories, Starports, Gateways, Stargates, Robotics Facilities and Hatcheries you had started by then.
help.productionForIncome: Production buildings you had, against how many your mining at 10 minutes could keep busy making units nonstop. 100% means enough to spend it all.
help.scoutTime: When one of your units first got near an enemy's starting base.
help.secondBase: When you started your second base. A town hall close to one you already have, like a Hatchery built for larvae, isn't a base of its own.
help.supply: When you first had that much supply in use.
help.supplyBlocked: How long you couldn't make units because you were out of supply, for every 10 minutes played. The first 3 minutes are left out, since early blocks are often part of a build, and so is time maxed out.
help.thirdBase: When you started your third base. A town hall close to one you already have, like a Hatchery built for larvae, isn't a base of its own.
help.unitsPerProduction: Army units you started each minute, for each production building you had, which shows how often they sat idle. Zerg count each larva once, so a pair of Zerglings is one. Units morphed from others, like Lurkers and Archons, don't count.
help.unspent: Minerals and gas you had banked, on average. Lower means you spent faster.
help.workerLead: Your workers minus your opponent's at 8 minutes. Below 0 means they were ahead.
help.workerProduction: The share of the first 8 minutes your Command Centers or Nexuses spent making workers, each from when it was done.
help.workers: Finished workers you had at that point.
help.workersLostRate: Workers of yours that died, for every 10 minutes you played, so a player who left early doesn't look careful.

names.body: Your names tell your games apart from downloaded replays. You can change them in Settings.
names.label: Your player names
names.title: Which of these names are you?

startup.body: GG Stats analyzes your games while it's running. Start it with Windows, in the tray, and none get missed. You can change this in Settings.
startup.label: Start with Windows
startup.title: Analyze every game you play?

rootErrorBoundary.reloadHint: Reloading usually fixes it. If it keeps happening, copy the details into a bug report.
rootErrorBoundary.title: Something went wrong

playerNames.askTitle: Which of these names are you?
playerNames.description: Replays don't say which player was you. Add the names you play under, on any account, to see your record and My stats. With none, games show both sides evenly.
playerNames.empty: No names yet. Stats are not tracked.
playerNames.foundBody: These names show up in a lot of your replays. Pick the ones that are you.
playerNames.title: Your names

replays.autoCapture: Analyze each game when it ends
replays.autoCaptureDescription: When a game ends, its replay is analyzed in the background. Replays StarCraft didn't save to AutoSave are kept in a GG Stats folder next to your replays.
replays.autoCaptureNotifications: Notify me when a game is analyzed while GG Stats is in the tray
replays.foldersDescription: Removing a folder takes its replays and their bookmarks out of the library.
replays.liveGame: Show who's in the games you join
replays.liveGameDescription: When you join a game, Live game shows who you play with and against, from what StarCraft and ShieldBattery keep on your computer. It only reads and listens, so your game isn't affected.
replays.quickOpen: Skip the preview when opening a replay file
replays.title: Replays

system.checkForUpdates: Check GitHub for new versions and install them
system.title: System

errors.save: There was an issue saving the settings.

ffaColors.poolHint: Minimum 8 colors, so every player always gets a unique color.
ffaColors.selfSetHint: You'll always get this color in games without teams. It's set aside so other players don't take it.
ffaColors.selfUnsetHint: You'll get a color from the pool, just like everyone else.
ffaColors.title: Individual color overrides

teamColors.description: How player colors appear in your games. Cycle between modes in game with Shift+Tab.
teamColors.editHint: Click a color to change it, or drag to reorder.
teamColors.label: Color overrides

mode.presetEverywhereDesc: Your color scheme on units and the minimap.
mode.presetOnMinimapDesc: Your color scheme on the minimap only.

teamColors.offNote: Off. The individual colors below are used in every game.
teamColors.overridesOffNote: Overrides are off, but your color scheme below is kept. Press Shift+Tab in game to turn overrides on at any time.
teamColors.poolOrderedHint: Colors are used in order, from the left.
teamColors.poolShuffledHint: These colors are used in a random order each game.
teamColors.selectCustomHint: Select the Custom preset to edit colors.
teamColors.selfFirstAllyHint: You'll get the first ally color.
teamColors.selfOverrideSetHint: You'll always be this color in team games.
teamColors.selfShuffleHint: You'll get a random color from your team's pool each game.
teamColors.title: Team color overrides

teamColorUsage.alwaysDesc: Your 1v1 opponent always gets the first enemy color.
teamColorUsage.alwaysShuffledDesc: Your 1v1 opponent gets a random color from your enemy pool.
teamColorUsage.exceptIn1v1Desc: Two player games use individual colors instead.
teamColorUsage.neverDesc: Everyone keeps their own color, even when alliances change.
teamColorUsage.title: Use team colors

input.grabPanTooltip: Adjusts how fast the camera moves when panning with the middle mouse button. When disabled, matches the legacy StarCraft: Remastered behavior.
input.hardwareCursorTooltip: Recommended for best performance and input responsiveness
input.legacyCursorSizingTooltip: Uses the original StarCraft: Remastered cursor sizes, which have inconsistent scales at higher resolutions.
input.legacySettingsDescription: These settings are available for compatibility with the StarCraft: Remastered settings, but are not recommended for use because they cause performance issues.
input.title: Input
